Federal Public Investment in Mexico, 1959–1963

Descriptive statistics — institutions and states (Cuadros 15–23, Inversión Pública Federal)

TapadosPRI

July 02, 2026

Overview

This report summarises federal public investment recorded in the yearly cuadros “Inversión de las dependencias, organismos y empresas del sector público, por entidades federativas” for 1959–1963. Each observation is one institution’s investment in one state in one year. All figures are reported in real millones de pesos, constant 1960 prices, deflated with the World Bank consumer price index (see below).

Deflation. Nominal pesos are converted to constant 1960 pesos using the Mexican CPI (World Bank WDI), rebased so 1960 = 100. Because the series begins in 1960, fiscal year 1959 is assigned the 1960 price level. Inflation was low in this window (≈3.4% cumulative 1960→1963), so the real adjustment is modest but makes the yearly totals directly comparable and consistent with the eventual 1925–2000 panel.

Presidency note. All five fiscal years fall within a single sexenio — Adolfo López Mateos (PRI, Dec 1958 – Nov 1964). “By presidency” cuts below therefore describe López Mateos’ term; the code carries a general year→president map so the same tables extend automatically if earlier cuadros (back to 1925) are added.

Recommended further analysis

  • Deflator robustness. Figures are now real (CPI, 1960 = 100). A wholesale or gross-fixed-capital-formation deflator (INEGI/Banxico) is arguably better for investment than the CPI and would be a useful sensitivity check; the WPI series here is empty before ~1970, so it can only anchor the later panel.
  • Per-capita and per-area allocation. Join 1960-census state population to see whether high totals (Federal District, Coahuila) survive normalisation, or whether poorer states received more per head — the real distributive question.
  • Extend the panel to 1925–1963. The full volume covers earlier cuadros; adding them turns the president lookup into a genuine cross-sexenio comparison (Cárdenas → Ávila Camacho → Alemán → Ruiz Cortines → López Mateos).
  • Volatility of allocations. Coefficient of variation of each state’s yearly share flags politically “swing” vs. stable recipients.
  • Link to the biography networks (project payoff). Cross the leading institutions here (SOP, SRH, PEMEX, CFE) with the govt_positions careers: did tapados and their network alters cluster in the highest-investment ministries? Use total_mdp from federal_investment_institutions.csv as a budget-based institution-importance weight for the manual rank tables in data/rank/.
  • Regional politics. Aggregate to regions (North, Bajío, Centre, South-East) and test whether investment tracked governors’ alignment with the president.
